title: "The objective and the brief: what a Kapso build takes"
sidebarTitle: "The brief"
description: "A build takes a brief: the objective, how it is measured, the baseline, the target, the rules and the budget, in one file the judge reads whole. How to write one, and what each line does."
keywords: ["kapso brief", "kapso-brief.md", "objective", "success criteria", "measurable goal", "kapso build"]

A build takes a brief. The brief says what to build, how success is
measured, where you start, where you want to end, what must never happen,
and how much to spend. The judge reads it whole: every experiment is scored
against it, and the campaign stops when the objective reads as met.

```text examples/churn-first-build/kapso-brief.md
Objective    Raise the churn model's out-of-sample ROC AUC above 0.85
             without changing the prediction contract: predict.py keeps
             writing id,churn_probability for every holdout id.
Measured by  kapso_evaluation/evaluate.py, ROC AUC on the held-out rows
Baseline     0.797 (the shipped logistic regression, bootstrap SE 0.010)
Target       0.85
Rules
  - the evaluator is never modified
  - no fitting on the holdout rows: their labels sit under the protected `kapso_evaluation/private/`, the evaluator's alone
Budget       minutes=45 experiments=3
```

```bash
kapso build --brief kapso-brief.md --evaluation evaluation --data data --repo repo --output campaign --detach
```

```python
from kapso import Kapso, Brief

solution = Kapso().build(
    Brief.read("kapso-brief.md"),
    evaluation="evaluation", data="data", repo="repo", output="build",
)
```

## What each line does

| Line | What it is for | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `Objective` | What to build, in as many lines as it takes. A number in it is what the judge checks | yes |
| `Measured by` | The evaluator (`kapso_evaluation/evaluate.py` when you pass one), or the protocol a campaign-built evaluator must follow: data, split, seed, metric | no |
| `Baseline` | Where the starting code stands: a figure you measured or one the repository records, named with its source. A build needs none, since its first evaluation is the first measurement; leave the line out when you have no figure | no |
| `Target` | The number that ends the campaign. Given, or proposed with headroom and said so | no |
| `Rules` | Invariants the judge enforces on every candidate: the evaluator untouched, no fitting on the hold-out, no rows dropped, data read-only | no |
| `Budget` | `minutes`, `experiments`, `usd` (model spend), `reserve_minutes` (escrowed for the final checkout and evaluation) | no |
| `Harness` | The [harness](/docs/harnesses) the build loads: a bundled name, a directory read from where the build runs, or a git reference. `--harness` wins over it | no |
| `Experience` | The [experience](/docs/experience) the build is served: `mine`, `mine:all`, `leeroopedia`, a bank path or git reference, an index name, as `- ` items or one comma-separated line. `--experience` and `load_experience()` win over it | no |

A line starts with its name; indented lines continue it, and a blank line
between two lines of the same field is a paragraph break. `Rules` and
`Experience` take `- ` items. `Budget` takes `name=value` tokens. An
unknown or repeated name, a missing objective, or a line that belongs to
no field is refused with its line number, never guessed at. The full
grammar is in the [brief format reference](/docs/reference/brief-format).

## A sentence is a brief too

`kapso build --goal "..."` and `build("...")` take a sentence and make a
brief with only an objective. Use it for a quick run; use the file when
the task has a measurement, a baseline or rules, which is most tasks worth
an hour of experiments.

## Three cases, by what you have

- **An evaluator.** Put the metric and the target in the brief and pass
  the evaluator with `--evaluation`. It is protected: a candidate that
  edits it is rejected and unscored. Add `Baseline` when you have the
  starting code's figure; when one run of the evaluator is cheap, that run
  gives it to you, and when it costs an hour, a GPU or paid calls, leave
  the line out and let the campaign's first evaluation be the first number.
  The plugin never runs it for you before you approve the brief.
- **A success criterion, no evaluator.** Write the protocol under
  `Measured by`: the data, the split, the seed, the metric and how it is
  printed. The campaign's first node builds the evaluator from it, the judge
  checks it is fair, and from then on it is protected like one you wrote.
  See [Evaluation](/docs/build/evaluation).
- **Nothing yet.** Write the objective and the best measurement you can
  name, and `Target` as `maximise within budget`. The campaign measures
  first: its first evaluation is the starting point every later one is
  read against.

## Rules, not methods

Rules go in the brief; methods do not. The judge holds every candidate to a
rule for the whole campaign, so "the evaluator is never modified" and "no
fitting on the hold-out" belong there. "Use gradient boosting" would be
frozen the same way, and the point of a campaign is to find out whether
something else does better.

## Targets with headroom

A target the data cannot reach ends in `max_iterations`, not in a result.
When you know the ceiling, leave room below it; when you do not, say in the
brief that the target is proposed, and read the first measurement before
raising it.

## What the judge sees

The whole brief, rendered as the text above, becomes the campaign's goal:
the judge scores every candidate against it and decides when to stop, and
the checkpoint fingerprints those exact bytes so a resume continues the
same brief. Nothing is clipped on the way, whatever its length.
